execution.description: Graphite's battery-only pod scoring moved behind a challenge-neutral ChallengeScoring port with battery as its first scoring. OWNER-GRAPHITE-TEST-WAVE-02 §3's pod worker-timeout rule is implemented: host-observed timing and lifecycle decide, pod files are evidence only, one retry, and repeated host-confirmed timeouts are an unscored candidate resource outcome.

expected: Battery's bytes stay unchanged through the port and the Attacker keeps working. The timeout rule can be enforced from evidence the candidate cannot write.
observed: Battery moved without a byte changing. Defaulting to the only registered scoring, and refusing unnamed calls once a second registers, kept every Attacker call and monkeypatch working with no battery literal in Graphite. The evidence rule had a sharper consequence than the brief. The pinned EV4 study image runs the bootstrap, the supervisor and the program as one non-root user, so the supervisor's failure.json, its exit code and the /status server are all reachable by the program. No pod-side signal can be authority, and that holds for program failures as much as timeouts. A pod-claimed program failure became FAILED_INFRA (candidate_failure_unattributed) rather than CANDIDATE_FAILED. Host timing had to be built from the host's own poll times: a lower bound (last running poll minus first) confirms a timeout, and an upper bound (end poll minus the last pre-running poll) exposes an impossible claim. The span includes Carbon's own compile and pin check, so it can over-credit by that pre-run time and never under-credit. Three regressions surfaced only in tests: mutation tests that patched a renamed seam or an old signature, a test pinned to a module constant this PR made unused and removed, and a Black/ruff format disagreement on one assertion. The first canonical run caught the removed constant after the native run had passed; the native run predated the removal.
keep: Move a Challenge's code behind a port by delegation, keeping every old call form, and pin byte-identity with tests on the moved values.
Make a no-name default refuse once it becomes ambiguous, instead of choosing a Challenge in shared code.
Decide what a pod's image actually separates before deciding which evidence can classify, and keep the admissible path behind a host-side record, never the pod's claim.
Confirm a failure that a teammate reports as 'already on main' on a detached main checkout before excluding it from a result.
change: Grep tests for a module attribute before removing an import that looks unused; tests and other agents' adapters pin public names.
Rerun the canonical suite on the exact head being pushed after any edit, however small.
Write assertions so Black and ruff format agree: bind a long right-hand side to a local first.
protocol_elements: construction scoring on Carbon's pods is one ChallengeScoring per Challenge, with no silent default
a pod run is typed by host-observed timing and lifecycle; pod-side files are evidence only
a worker timeout is retried once before any candidate outcome, and the retry is charged to the run
a pod image's supervisor/program separation is a host-side record, verified before any report is admissible
